Finding: The dedicated Leaders page still exposes sale-oriented content and live structured data after registration was marked unavailable.
Evidence: The page still has four live JSON-LD Course/Offer objects, a visible '$499 / class' hero, a live Leadership Cohort anchor, private Leadership-track sales copy, and FAQs describing individual-session pricing/capacity.
Impact: Direct visitors and search crawlers can still be told that Leaders products are active, contradicting the cohort-only decision and Phase 3 requirement.
Recommended fix: Comment out the remaining hero/sales/team/FAQ copy or replace the page body with the unavailable message; remove or archive the live Leaders Course/Offer structured data while preserving recoverable source.

Finding: The homepage hero still advertises the paused individual-class products and prices.
Evidence: Live stat labels say 'beginner classes - $129 each or $395 for all' and 'intermediate classes - $199 each or $995 for all'. These lines are outside the commented catalog block.
Impact: Visitors still receive an explicit individual-purchase message even though those products are not in the catalog.
Recommended fix: Change the stats to cohort-only language such as '4-week Beginner cohort - $395' and '6-week Intermediate cohort - $995'.

Finding: The live classes page still describes individual-session capacity as part of the public offering.
Evidence: The over-capacity copy says '(9 for cohorts, 12 for individual sessions)' and refers to the 'public track'.
Impact: This creates stale expectations about a paused live format and weakens the cohort-only positioning.
Recommended fix: Remove the individual-session reference and describe only cohort caps, or explicitly label any private team engagement as a separate inquiry-only service.

Finding: The homepage JSON-LD registration answer still tells crawlers to choose classes rather than a cohort.
Evidence: The live JSON-LD answer says 'Browse the class catalog, choose your classes, and click Register', while the visible FAQ was changed to 'pick your cohort'.
Impact: Search/AEO output is inconsistent with the visible page and can imply individual checkout remains available.
Recommended fix: Make the JSON-LD answer match the visible cohort-only wording.

Finding: The quiz does not preserve the original individual recommendation records verbatim.
Evidence: The paused records were replaced with comments containing desc: '...' instead of their original descriptions.
Impact: This violates the preservation requirement and loses recoverable content from the quiz source, making restoration incomplete.
Recommended fix: Restore the exact original records as line-commented JavaScript, or archive the exact records before keeping them commented out.

Finding: The active Beginner quiz record does not use the exact catalog product name.
Evidence: The quiz uses 'AI Beginners 4-Week Bundle'; the live catalog key is 'AI Beginners 4-Week Bundle (cohort)'.
Impact: Any future code that uses the quiz record name as a catalog key will fail closed; it also violates the plan's exact-name requirement.
Recommended fix: Use 'AI Beginners 4-Week Bundle (cohort)' in the active quiz record.

Finding: The quiz fallback recommends only one cohort for ambiguous answers instead of showing both active cohorts.
Evidence: When no trigger fires, fallbackTier/fallbackCohort selects Beginner for total <= 12 and Intermediate otherwise; it renders one card only.
Impact: Neutral or ambiguous users are not shown both cohort options as required by Phase 6, and the recommendation may be arbitrary.
Recommended fix: Render both active cohort cards in the no-trigger fallback, or document and implement a non-ambiguous rule that satisfies the requirement.

Finding: Required restructure changes are uncommitted even though the decision log says all nine phases are committed.
Location: git status; about.html; contact.html; tools.html; classes.html; newsletter.html; articles/* listed by git status; class-checkout/leaders.html
Evidence: The worktree has 14 modified files. Most are the remaining Phase 3 nav/CTA changes; class-checkout/leaders.html contains the empty generated schedule blocks. None are included in the Phase 3 or Phase 7 commits.
Impact: A deployment or review based on HEAD alone will omit required changes, and the repository cannot reproduce the claimed shipped state.
Recommended fix: Review the uncommitted changes, commit the intended Phase 3/7 files in a dedicated commit, then update the status only after the committed tree matches the audit.

Finding: The schedule-entry archive has a .json extension but is not valid JSON.
Evidence: The file begins with an HTML comment and YAML-style section headings, followed by multiple standalone JSON objects rather than one JSON document.
Impact: Archive consumers may reasonably expect a parseable JSON file and fail; the archive is less mechanically recoverable than intended.
Recommended fix: Use a .txt/.md archive for the mixed format, or make it valid JSON with metadata and removedEntries arrays.

Finding: The required live/preview Stripe walkthrough is not evidenced by the repository audit.
Evidence: Static checks confirm two live catalog entries and valid JavaScript, but there is no evidence of a browser walkthrough or successful test-mode checkout for both cohorts.
Impact: The most important end-to-end purchase path remains unverified; date selection, Netlify routing, Stripe mode, and deployed environment behavior could still fail.
Recommended fix: Run the owner walkthrough in the deployed preview/test environment for both cohort products and record the result, including the checkout session names/prices.
